dedupe_keys.name: vanuatu earthquake of december 2024 coordination of national and international emergency medical teams

description: This case study reports how emergency medical teams were coordinated after the magnitude 7.3 earthquake that struck Vanuatu on 17 December 2024, affecting over 80,000 people with 14 deaths and 265 injuries. The authors, from the Vanuatu Ministry of Health, the World Health Organization and its Western Pacific office, the Japan International Cooperation Agency and Japanese, American and other hospitals and universities, published it in 2026 in Western Pacific Surveillance and Response, free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Vanuatu's health system is dispersed and short of specialists and had recent cyclone damage. Within 24 hours the Vanuatu Medical Assistance Team, the national emergency medical team set up in 2017, was activated and set up an Emergency Medical Team Coordination Cell in the national health emergency operations centre; teams from Australia, Fiji, Indonesia, Japan and New Zealand followed, and the WHO emergency medical team Minimum Data Set was used to monitor health trends. Coverage is national. Caveats: the report is a practitioner account, and the minimum data set records are not public. Eight national and international teams worked alongside local services and reported more than 5,500 consultations to the coordination cell, including specialised mental health support. Simulation uses: surge staffing and coordination patterns for health emergency response models in small island states. Related records: the Vanuatu evacuation centre tracking system (data-decm-cluster-vanuatu-evacuation-centre-tracking) covers the same country's displacement response.
